constraints_found.source_line: Eleven attempts. Every one unrolled itself on the way to the plate. I would now like to eat some made by a professional.

constraints_found.constraint: Strict diet: vegetarian, needs a whole menu section with no fish or meat (deal-breaker)
constraints_found.source_line: Mina, I've already ruled places out for you. Same standard as sushi day: a whole part of the menu with no fish and no meat in it, so you can point at anything.

constraints_found.constraint: Allergy: peanut (deal-breaker), for someone in the group
constraints_found.source_line: good. the satay incident stays a one-off. that story doesn't get a sequel, whatever sauce it comes in

constraints_found.constraint: Budget: $$ ($$$ is one tier over and costs a star, not a deal-breaker)
constraints_found.source_line: my turn. the trip fund finished its job, so i'm officially a two-dollar-sign person now / three signs won't sink me anymore. but i will bring it up at every dinner...
could we find somewhere calm and hushed, where nobody has to shout across the table?

constraints_found.constraint: Preference: simple and light, nothing deep-fried
constraints_found.source_line: and in return, my one ask for the food: simple and light. nothing that's been battered and dunked in hot oil

elimination.waterfront_spindrift: Fits everything: sushi, $$, hushed counter, full fish-and-meat-free page (kelp/mushroom miso), no fryer, peanut-safe (toasted rice crunch, soy/ponzu). 3 stars.
elimination.waterfront_starboard: Deal-breaker: veg page dressed in white miso with roasted peanuts, spinach in crushed peanuts.
elimination.waterfront_gull_point: Deal-breaker: nothing vegetarian (eel sauce on veg nigiri, salmon in cucumber roll).
elimination.waterfront_mooring_post: Safe but $$$, one over budget: 2 stars.
elimination.waterfront_ropewalk: Safe but loud (bells, shouting, loud playlist): misses calm, 2 stars.
elimination.waterfront_halyard: Safe but everything is tempura/fried: misses light, 2 stars.
elimination.waterfront_cormorant: Safe, quiet, light, but Greek, not sushi: misses craving, 2 stars.

notes: The peanut allergy is only signalled via the 'satay incident' callback plus Cyrus binning a peanut dressing; a first-time player without memory of earlier levels might not know whose allergy it is, though the intent is clear enough. Starboard is a good trap for players who skim past the second half of its review.
Maya's budget lines are well calibrated: '$$ person' plus 'three signs won't sink me' reads clearly as $$$ = one-star penalty, not a deal-breaker.

Each decoy fails exactly one constraint, which makes the puzzle clean. Spindrift's reviews map almost one-to-one onto the constraints (hush, veg page, no fryer, peanut families), so once constraints are found the answer is fairly obvious.
